item.title: Philippines: Floods - Aug 2026
item.description:
Affected country: Philippines
Glide: FL-2026-000169-PHL

The Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) has intensified over the Philippines, bringing persistent and at times heavy to intense rainfall over western and northern Luzon, Metro Manila, and parts of MIMAROPA and the Visayas. The enhanced monsoon is being further influenced by an two LPAs east of Extreme Northern Luzon, which may develop into a tropical cyclone and is expected to continue enhancing the Habagat. As of 29 August 2026, PAGASA has issued multiple heavy rainfall warnings, including Red Warning over parts of Metro Manila and Occidental Mindoro, with serious flooding and landslides possible in affected areas. (IFRC & Philippine Red Cross, 29 Aug 2026)

The latest cumulative National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) Situational Report no. 27 from 30 August reported 7,467,238 people affected, with more than 1,500 areas flooded since the beginning of August. With combined damages to agriculture and infrastructure, the full cost is estimated at over 8 billion pesos (over 100 million CHF). 32 people have died and 17 injured by monsoon-related incidents. [...] According to NDRRMC, a total of 26,197 families (93,636 people) have been displaced, with 43,175 people temporarily taking shelter inside 529 evacuation centres as of 30 August. Almost 66,000 farmers and fisherfolk have been affected, and almost 60,000 hectares of Crops have suffered damages with around 10,000 hectares destroyed. In total the Agricultural sector has suffered estimated damages of over 2 billion pesos. (IFRC, 2 Sep 2026)

item.title: Nepal: Flash Floods - Aug 2026
item.description:
Affected countries: China, Nepal
Glide: FF-2026-000162-NPL

A major flash flood struck Rasuwa district after a sudden and intense surge of water entered the Bhote Koshi River from the Tibet (China) side at approximately 9:15 AM [on 26 August 2026]. The flood rapidly impacted the Timure, Rasuwagadhi, and Syabrubesi areas, causing significant damage to settlements, markets, police infrastructure, roads, and hydropower facilities. Authorities have warned that rising water levels could affect downstream communities along the Trishuli River corridor. (IFRC, 26 Aug 2026)

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), 10,000 households require immediate relief. At least 157 deaths have been confirmed and nearly 245 people remain missing, including security personnel, customs officials, foreign tourists and residents, while search and rescue operations continue. (WFP, 27 Aug 2026)

Five days after the flash flood of the Trishuli River swept through Raswuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, the Government of Nepal’s response efforts continue at scale, with more than 10,000 people rescued and over 20,000 personnel mobilised for search and rescue operations, while authorities report 903 fatalities and 4,247 people still missing. The Government has officially declared a flood emergency in 15 municipalities and designated two additional municipalities as impacted, underscoring the scale of humanitarian needs across the affected areas. (OCHA, 31 Aug 2026)

The Rasuwa floods have claimed 1,003 lives, with 3,916 people still out of contact and 11,814 rescued (NDRRMA, 1 September, 13:00). 3,458 displaced people are living in 27 displacement sites in Nuwakot and Rasuwa, mostly in schools. Parts of Tarkeshwar (Nuwakot) have received no assistance, all wards of Aamachhodingmo (Rasuwa) remain inaccessible by road, and four rural municipalities in Dhading lack safe drinking water. Access remains the main constraint. While relief supplies are available, damaged infrastructure, including 41 destroyed bridges and blocked highways, is limiting delivery to remote communities. Following a joint Resident Coordination Office, OCHA, and WFP mission to Nuwakot on 31 August, partners are establishing a coordination hub in Bidur to strengthen operational coordination and address response gaps. (OCHA, 1 Sep 2026)

item.title: Indonesia: Earthquake - Aug 2026
item.description:
Affected country: Indonesia
Glide: EQ-2026-000150-IDN

A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck offshore Nagekeo Regency, East Nusa Tenggara Province, on 15 August 2026 at 04:58 WIB. The earthquake occurred at a depth of 15 km, approximately 38 km northeast of Mbay. The tsunami warning issued for several coastal areas was officially lifted by BMKG at 07:31 WIB. As of 16 August 2026 at 00:00 WIB, BNPB reported 47 fatalities and 101 injuries. More than 5,000 people remain displaced, including 3,356 people in Sikka, 2,078 in Manggarai, and 500 in Nagekeo. Additional displacement was reported in Bima and the Selayar Islands. Preliminary assessments recorded 914 houses severely damaged, 126 moderately damaged, and 317 slightly damaged. At least 93 educational facilities, 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices were also affected. BMKG recorded 341 aftershocks with magnitudes ranging from 2.5 to 6.2. Continuing aftershocks, damaged roads, electricity outages, and communication disruptions are affecting assessments and humanitarian operations. The Larantuka–Maumere road is accessible, while the Ende–Nagekeo road remains cut off. (IFRC & PMI, 16 Aug 2026)

The number of IDPs increased to 9,290 people, based on the BNPB update at 00.00 WIB. The details include 3,356 Sikka people—1,356 in the Samador GOR and 2,000 spread independently in 10 points—Manggarai 2,078 people, and Nagekeo 500 people. [...] The earthquake shock was followed by 341 aftershock activities. The number of fatalities recorded to date is 47 people, with the highest death toll in Manggarai Regency with 23 people and East Manggarai with 17 people. Meanwhile, other fatalities were spread across Sikka Regency with 4 people, West Manggarai with 1 person, Ende with 1 person, and Nagekeo with 1 person. At least 101 residents were reported injured with varying degrees of severity. Damage increased significantly compared to previous reports: BNPB now records 914 houses severely damaged, 126 moderately damaged, and 317 lightly damaged—a total of 1,357 houses. The affected facilities include 93 educational facilities, 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices. (MPBI, 17 Aug 2026)

As of 18 August 2026, 69 people were reported dead and 1,199 injured, including 115 people with serious injuries and 1,084 with minor injuries. A total of 46,252 people remain displaced, including 46,181 people across the seven affected regencies in East Nusa Tenggara and 71 people in Bima Regency, West Nusa Tenggara. [...] Preliminary damage included 5,713 houses severely damaged, 2,098 moderately damaged and 3,402 slightly damaged. A further 283 educational facilities, 211 health facilities, 97 government buildings, 96 places of worship and 106 business premises or offices were affected. (IFRC & PMI, 18 Aug 2026)

according to BNPB, emergency response period for M7.7 Earthquake in East Nusa Tenggara has been extended until 12 September 2026, while response and early recovery operations remain ongoing. Authorities continue to focus on emergency assistance while accelerating rehabilitation and reconstruction planning in affected areas. As of 31 August at 0900H UTC+7, BNPB records 120 fatalities, 1,658 injured persons, and approximately 188,673 displaced persons. (AHA Centre, 30 Aug 2026)

item.title: Colombia: Earthquake - Aug 2026
item.description:
Affected country: Colombia
Glide: EQ-2026-000146-COL

According to information from the Colombian Geological Service (SGC), an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 was recorded on Monday, August 10, 2026, in the morning, with its epicenter in the town of San José del Palmar, in the department of Chocó, located on the Colombian Pacific coast, at a depth of 82 kilometers.

Although the epicenter was in the department of Chocó, direct impacts were also felt in the departments of Caldas, Risaralda, and Valle del Cauca. Preliminary reports from media outlets and municipal governments indicate damage in the capitals and other municipalities of these departments: in Valle de Cauca, 3 people were injured in El Cairo and 2 died in El Zarzal, in addition to the collapse of 20 buildings and minor structural damage to 2 hospitals; in Risaralda, 18 people died; and in Chocó, 10 people were injured and 3 are missing. The number of people affected in the area continues to rise, and the President of the Republic has established a Unified Command Post. (Cruz Roja Colombiana & IFRC, 10 Aug 2026)

item.title: Myanmar: Floods - Jul 2026
item.description:
Affected country: Myanmar
Glide: FL-2026-000141-MMR

Heavy and continuous monsoon rainfall caused rising water levels and flooding across low-lying and flood-prone areas of Ayeyarwady Region. The situation escalated on 30 July 2026, when an embankment near Myit Kyo Village in Laymyatna Township breached, and floodwaters rapidly entered Laymyatna town and surrounding communities. The flooding has affected residential areas, agricultural land, roads, and public infrastructure, with communities along the Ngawun River being particularly affected. Water levels in the Ngawun River have exceeded the danger level and remain elevated, with further rainfall potentially worsening the situation.

The Myanmar Red Cross Society (MRCS) Regional Branch started the response with its own resources on 1 August 2026, and the information indicates impacts across 5 wards, 23 village tracts, and 122 villages in Laymyatna Township; 2 wards, 16 village tracts, and 14 villages in Yegyi Township; and 10 village tracts and 33 villages in Hinthada Township. The most significant impacts are in Laymyethna, Yegyi, and Hinthada Townships, among other townships in Ayeyarwady, particularly communities located along the Ngawun River and other low-lying areas. [...] Approximately 8,907 households, representing 28,455 people, had been affected and displaced to 28 evacuation camps, including community centres, schools, temporary shelters, and monasteries. (IFRC, 17 Aug 2026)

item.title: Afghanistan: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
item.description:
Affected country: Afghanistan
Glide: FF-2026-000120-AFG

Heavy and continuous rainfall on 20 July triggered flash flooding in several areas of eastern Afghanistan. The impacts have varied significantly between locations with the most severe impacts reported in Parun City, Nuristan Province, alongside flooding in Torkham, Nangarhar Province, and Alingar District, Laghman Province. Parun City was severely affected by a sudden flash flood at approximately 15:00 hrs on 20 July. So far 23 people have been confirmed dead, 15 have been injured with others reported missing. Search and rescue operations are ongoing. (OCHA, 21 Jul 2026)

According to preliminary information compiled by the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS), more than 910 families were affected. The floods caused 31 deaths and 11 injuries, with 77 cases of missing persons reported. Shelter damage was significant, with 910 houses completely and partially damaged, particularly in several provinces of Nuristan, Laghman, Parwan, Logar, Kabul, Kapisa, Panjsher, Nangarhar, Ghazni, Khost ,Maidan Wardak, Paktika and Paktia provinces. In addition, the floods had a severe impact on livelihoods, resulting in the loss of 330 livestock and damage to approximately 5240 jeribs of agricultural land, further increasing vulnerabilities among farming and pastoral households. (ARCS & IFRC, 25 Jul 2026)

Beyond Nuristan, flooding and landslides damaged shelter, agricultural land, irrigation systems, education infrastructure and livelihood assets across the affected provinces. Laghman, initially reported as having sustained no residential damage, was confirmed by 28 July to have 187 families affected, 183 houses damaged or destroyed, approximately 800 acres of seasonal crops lost and some 310 livestock lost or damaged. In Paktika, flooding destroyed 14 houses, killed 37 livestock and washed away approximately 122 hectares of agricultural land. Public schools and community-based education facilities were damaged across Nangarhar, Kunar, Nuristan and Laghman. Flooding and landslides may also have displaced or exposed explosive ordnance, creating a secondary hazard for affected communities and responders. (IFRC, 6 Aug 2026)

On 3 August, a second flash flood struck Barg-e-Matal district in eastern Nuristan, affecting 191 houses, which were either destroyed or damaged. The floods also damaged bridges, roads, flood protection walls, agricultural land and water supply networks. In the Central Region, flash floods across nine provinces resulted in two fatalities and six injuries. A total of 316 houses were affected, impacting 2,057 people. Approximately 1.6 million square meters of agricultural land were damaged, around 300 livestock were killed, and 17 schools sustained damage, further affecting livelihoods and access to basic services. A separate flooding incident in Paktia province destroyed 11 houses and damaged agricultural land. (UNICEF, 21 Aug 2026)
